chunks: As for what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated — from Abu Ja'far, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, from his father, from his forefathers, from 'Ali (peace be upon him):

he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) said: 'If the martyr dies on that same day or the next day, bury him in his garments. But if he lingers for several days until his wounds change in condition, he shall be given the ritual bath (ghusl).'

This is a report that conforms to the Sunni position; we do not act upon it. For we have demonstrated that if the slain person did not die on the battlefield, his ghusl is obligatory — whether [his wounds] changed in condition or not. The practice must follow this ruling. It also conforms to what we have mentioned in our major book [al-Mabsut], where we treated the matter exhaustively.

key_terms.الشَّهِيدُ: martyr, one killed in battle on the path of Allah
key_terms.الْمَعْرَكَةِ: the battlefield, the direct site of armed combat
key_terms.غُسِّلَ: was given the ritual bath (ghusl), a purification rite for the deceased
key_terms.لِلْعَامَّةِ: conforming to the 'generality' (Sunni majority) — technical Shia hadith criterion signalling a report's unreliability

ai.seo_question: Does a martyr who does not die directly on the battlefield require ghusl according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through a chain from Imam 'Ali (AS) who cites the Prophet (SAWW), rules that a martyr who dies on the day of battle or the next day is buried in his garments without ghusl, but if he lingers for several days until his wounds alter in condition, he must receive the ghusl. Shaykh al-Tusi explicitly rejects this report as conforming to the Sunni position — invoking the technical criterion muwafiq lil-'amma — and affirms the established Shia ruling that any slain person who did not die on the battlefield itself is obligatorily subject to ghusl, regardless of whether his wounds changed.
